content: Before starting any medication, including lactulose, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any allergies to the medication or its ingredients. This product may contain inactive components that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Lactulose contains various sugars, so if you have diabetes, it may affect your blood sugar levels. Regularly monitor your blood sugar as directed and share the results with your healthcare provider. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary, and it is not known whether it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Always maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal guidelines. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
